title: Playbook for SDK Quickstart Cohorts & Initiative Rollforward
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures an operational playbook and tracking surface for running cohort-based SDK + docs quickstart initiatives. The goal is to run three 4-week cohorts (JS, Python, and Server-side integration) to validate friction points, optimize time-to-first-call, and gather qualitative feedback to inform the broader DX roadmap. The playbook standardizes enrollment, experiment instrumentation, success signals, and rollforward decisions so results are comparable across cohorts and cycles.
updates: 2025-11-12: Scoping workshop with Eng, Design, Growth. Agreed on cohort cadence (4 weeks) and a reduced scope for cohort 1: JS SDK quickstart plus sample app.
2025-12-03: Prototype quickstart created (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstarts/js-starter). Demo to leadership passed — ask: add telemetry hooks for first-call path.
2026-01-07: Engineering uplift scheduled (ENG-40212) to add time-to-first-call tracking and funnel events to the DX analytics pipeline. ETA for instrumentation: 2026-01-21.
2026-01-25: Design reviewed quickstart flow; provided inline feedback on copy and checkpoint UX. Decision: include a 'run sample' CTA on README and a short video snippet in README.

2026-02-14: Run 1 (JS cohort) launched with 45 participants. Early metrics show 60% of cohorts hit first-call within 30 minutes; retention at day 7 is 28% (baseline needed). Collected 12 structured feedback responses.
2026-02-21: PM-PL review: prioritize localized README for cohort 2; translation backlog added to docs workstream.

2026-03-03: Trade-off discussion: add deeper prompt examples vs. keeping quickstart minimal. Decision: keep core quickstart minimal; provide 'advanced recipes' in a linked repo to avoid increasing time-to-first-call.
2026-03-08: UX sign-off on cohort survey and net-promoter style question set. Next: automate survey delivery after day 3 via product-marketing cadence.
2026-03-10: Rollforward proposal drafted: run cohort 2 (Python) with same instrumented metrics, split test README variants (video vs. screenshots).
acceptance_criteria: Cohort playbook document published with enrollment checklist and runbook
Instrumentation in place: time_to_first_call, first_successful_call_event, day_7_retention, survey_response_id
Run 3 cohorts (JS, Python, Server) completed with at least 30 participants each
Quantitative report produced comparing cohorts and recommending 3 concrete follow-up product changes
Template PRD for rollforward decisions with prioritization matrix mapped to effort and impact
risks: Telemetry gaps: if ENG analytics rollout (ENG-40212) slips, primary metrics will be unreliable
Engineering capacity: localization and video assets may require contractor support and delay cohort start
Selection bias: cohorts recruited from beta users and existing SDK adopters may not reflect new-user funnel
Confounding experiments: multiple concurrent doc changes may make attribution of improvements difficult
next_steps: Complete ENG-40212 telemetry work and validate events in staging (owner: Owen Martinez)
Finalize cohort 2 materials (Python quickstart + localized README) and schedule launch (owner: Design)
Create dashboard in Console for cohort metrics and share with stakeholders weekly
Implement automated day-3 and day-14 survey delivery and aggregate responses into Google Sheet for qualitative tagging
Prepare rollforward decision template and run prioritization session with PL by 2026-03-28
metrics: Activation rate: percent who make a first successful API call within 48 hours (target +20% vs baseline)
Time-to-first-call: median minutes from sign-up to successful call (target < 20 minutes)
Day-7 retention: percent of cohort with any activity within 7 days (target 35%+)
Qualitative NPS-style score from cohort survey (target >= 7/10)
Conversion to repeated usage or paid trial within 30 days (tracked via Console signals)
